correctness.rationale: For n≥5, the unsigned pair-incidence identity U^T U=(n-2)I+J implies the complete mean-zero Laplacian eigenspace decomposition, giving Q=D^T[(2(n-1))^{-1}I+(2n(n-1))^{-1}UU^T]D. A signed edge stabilizer has a two-parameter anti-invariant mean-zero gradient potential; every equivariant map into the cut space must be symmetric. Hence any equivariant cut projection equals the orthogonal one. For an equivariant cycle projection R, the transpose of its difference from the orthogonal cycle projection has range in the cut space and vanishes on it; symmetry forces this difference to vanish. Averaging over S_n then proves minimality among ALL projections for each ℓ_p. The five exhaustive adjacent-potential classes yield the two claimed endpoint rational formulas; the complementary diagonal identity gives the cycle formula. Every edge column was checked exactly for n=4,...,8 (24,980 rational assertions, including independent grounded-Laplacian entries for n≤7). Unrestricted numerical LPs agreed for n=4,5,6. No finite sample is treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The family n≥5 is not complete multipartite (unlike the previously covered n=4 boundary), not a Hamming graph, and not a complete or clique-prism graph. The highly relevant 2023 full text develops the invariant-projection framework but studies Hamming graphs and tori; its general uniqueness criterion does not provide the Johnson-family uniqueness argument or exact endpoint constants. Actual ranked-record searches with Johnson, triangular, line-graph, spectral and numerical aliases did not retrieve an equivalent cut/cycle edge-space formula. A Johnson spherical projector record concerns a distinct vertex-function subspace. This supports originality to current best knowledge, with bibliographic limitations noted.

value.rationale: The graph-edge projection constants govern linear complementability and graph transportation-cost geometry, the explicit context of the primary 2023 mathematical literature. J(n,2)=L(K_n) is a natural classical Johnson graph family distinct from the studied Hamming, toroidal, or balanced multipartite infinite families. Both exact relative cut and cycle constants are determined simultaneously for all n≥5, with a nontrivial signed-representation optimality proof, explicit sharp rational expressions, and different strict limiting regimes (3 and 4). This is a natural infinite-family invariant calculation, not an arbitrary finite slice or renaming of a known table.
